title: Mobile Solutions for Business Central: Why the Native App Is All You Need
summary: The native Business Central mobile app since version 23 offers barcode scanning, tablet support, and full AL extensibility, making expensive third-party mobile solutions unnecessary for most companies. This post explains why the fourth-generation native app is superior to legacy ADCS systems and dedicated third-party apps, covering practical implementation methods and real-world examples.
key_points: The native BC mobile app includes barcode scanning (camera or dedicated scanners like Zebra), tablet optimization, and full AL extensibility since version 23
Implementation can be as simple as setting ExtendedDatatype = Barcode on a field, or more complex using AL code for programmatic scanning and custom workflows
The native app avoids costs and maintenance burdens of third-party solutions - no middleware, no separate licensing, no vendor dependency, and upgrades work seamlessly
Mobile customizations use the same AL development process as desktop Business Central, deployed through Visual Studio Code with full IntelliSense and version control support

quotes.text: Since Business Central 2023 release wave 2 (version 23), Microsoft has included native barcode scanning in the mobile app.
quotes.why_it_matters: Marks the pivotal moment when the native app became a viable replacement for third-party solutions

quotes.text: The mobile app is fully extendable using AL - the same modern development language you use for all Business Central customizations.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that mobile customizations integrate seamlessly with core BC development workflows, eliminating separate tools and expertise

quotes.text: If you're buying a third-party mobile app in 2026, you're probably making a mistake.
quotes.why_it_matters: Challenges the conventional wisdom about mobile solutions and advocates for native-first approach
